payload.body:
You need a home life with enough privacy and consistency to understand what you are feeling without constantly responding to everybody else first. Familiar routines, the people you live with, the amount of noise around you, and knowing when your time is actually your own can affect you more deeply than other people may realize.

Belonging often comes through repetition for you. The meal you make without thinking, the person who knows when you need company and when to leave you alone, the morning routine that makes the day easier, or simply knowing who has access to your space can give you something you can rely on.

Familiarity can keep a bad setup in place. You keep hosting because everyone expects it, organize the household around somebody else's needs, or continue a family routine long after it has stopped working because changing it feels more serious than the inconvenience itself.

A home can change without becoming less meaningful. Pay attention to what actually sustains you and what you keep doing only because it is familiar. Care, privacy, access, money, and responsibility all need to be things the people living there can talk about and change.
